platform_failure.head: 813d9b0
platform_failure.original_test: standardization avoids overflowing a representable centered result
platform_failure.cause: colMeans accumulates in LDOUBLE before division; double-only accumulation overflows to infinity even though the mean is representable.

before.test_note: An earlier draft expected matching incidental row names; that expectation was corrected before this final before-run. Numerical expectations and the original failing macOS test were retained.

fixes: Keep finite colMeans centers unchanged; recompute only nonfinite centers after dividing by the largest absolute value.

For SD fallback, subtract the first value before normalization if differences are finite, preserving small separations near large offsets. Use global normalization when reference subtraction overflows.
scope: Finite ordinary centers and ordinary SD arithmetic remain unchanged, verified with exact equality.
Sparse adapters still delegate scaling to the engine; dense/sparse parity and independent native glmnet checks passed.
A true standard deviation above DBL_MAX is still rejected.
A midpoint between adjacent representable doubles cannot itself be represented as a stored double center; this fix does not promise exact centering beyond floating-point precision.

browser.accessibility_limit: Automated checks reported no violations; incomplete checks remain for manual interpretation. This is an implementer browser walkthrough, not a recruited usability study.
browser.counting_note: Counts are per runner, not distinct test scenarios or a combined coverage total. Explorer invokes chart and records one child-suite status; chart invokes frontier and cost_scale and records two child-suite statuses. Child assertion arrays are not copied into parent arrays. Reporting the sum as 4,608 independent checks was misleading because it includes those three wrapper assertions and repeated task families.
